title: Anthropic signs a $10bn compute deal with a week-old cloud startup
excerpt: Anthropic has signed a $10bn, six-year computing deal with Volta, a cloud startup that only just launched, adding yet another supplier to its list.
content_html:
Anthropic has found another place to buy computing power, and this time it is a company barely old enough to have a logo. The AI developer has signed a $10bn, six-year deal with Volta, a cloud startup that only just launched, according to Bloomberg.

The agreement is Volta’s marquee contract and, for Anthropic, one more supplier on an already crowded list. It is the kind of deal that has become routine for a company whose appetite for compute seems to have no ceiling.

Anthropic now buys capacity almost everywhere it can. Its biggest backer, Amazon, has put up to $25bn into the company and supplies much of its compute, and that is only the start of the list.

The rest reads like a roll-call of the industry. Anthropic struck its biggest compute deal yet with Google and Broadcom as its run rate reached $30bn, and it has leaned heavily on Google’s TPUs. While, AMD is investing $5bn and deploying two gigawatts of GPUs to run Claude, while CoreWeave, Akamai, and even SpaceX have all signed on to provide compute.

Volta is not even the only $10bn deal in the mix. Anthropic has been in talks with Meta over a compute agreement of the same size, a measure of how many suppliers it takes to feed a single frontier lab.

What makes the Volta deal stand out is how new the counterparty is. Anthropic is committing $10bn over six years to a startup founded this year, valued at $2.4bn, and only just out of stealth.

Volta’s idea is to make Nvidia’s chips affordable to more than the giants, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Altimeter, Nvidia, and Michael Dell. It plans to run Anthropic’s capacity partly through the bitcoin miner Bitdeer, starting at a site in Norway.

For Volta, the deal is validation and ballast at once. A $10bn anchor customer hands a days-old startup the credibility, and the cash flows, to raise and build against.

For Anthropic, spreading its compute across many suppliers is a form of insurance. No single provider can meet its needs, and depending too heavily on any one, including its own investors, carries risks of its own.

Diversifying is also about leverage; a lab that can shift workloads between Amazon, Google, AMD, and now a startup is less beholden to any one of them on price or priority.

Anthropic has even explored building its own chips, the logical end point for a company that has decided compute is too important to leave entirely to others.

The arrangements also feed a worry that has trailed the whole AI boom. Chipmakers and clouds increasingly help finance the customers who buy from them, an interlocking web that could magnify losses if demand disappoints.

The scale of it all is hard to fathom. Anthropic’s compute commitments now run to tens of billions of dollars, a bet that demand for Claude will keep climbing fast enough to justify the spend.

The spending tracks the business. Anthropic’s revenue has climbed sharply as Claude has won enterprise customers, which is what lets it sign commitments that would sink a smaller firm.

Committing $10bn to a days-old company is not without risk, either. Volta still has to build and deliver, and Anthropic is effectively wagering that a first-time operator can execute at a scale established clouds find hard.

The deal also hints at where the bottleneck now sits. Anthropic is chasing not just chips but the power and sites to run them, which is exactly what a firm like Volta, built by infrastructure financiers, is selling.

For a company racing to keep Claude ahead, the maths is simple. Capacity is the constraint, and Anthropic will take it wherever it can find it, even from a startup that did not exist a year ago.

content_html_zh:
Anthropic 找到了另一个购买算力的地方，这次是一家刚刚成立到没有徽标的公司。 据彭博社报道，这家人工智能开发商已与刚刚成立的云初创公司 Volta 签署了一份价值 100 亿美元、为期六年的协议。

该协议是 Volta 的招牌合同，对于 Anthropic 来说，是本已拥挤的名单上又一个供应商。 对于一家对计算的胃口似乎没有上限的公司来说，这种交易已经成为惯例。

Anthropic 现在几乎在所有可以购买的地方购买容量。 其最大的支持者亚马逊已向该公司注资高达 250 亿美元，并为其提供大部分计算服务，而这仅仅是清单的开始。

其余的内容读起来就像是行业的点名。 Anthropic 与谷歌和博通达成了迄今为止最大的计算交易，其运行率达到 300 亿美元，并且它严重依赖谷歌的 TPU。 与此同时，AMD 正在投资 50 亿美元并部署 2 千兆瓦的 GPU 来运行 Claude，而 CoreWeave、Akamai 甚至 SpaceX 都已签约提供计算。

Volta 甚至不是其中唯一一笔价值 100 亿美元的交易。 Anthropic 一直在与 Meta 就一项相同规模的计算协议进行谈判，该协议衡量一个前沿实验室需要多少供应商。

Volta 交易之所以引人注目，是因为交易对手是新人。 Anthropic 承诺在六年内向一家今年成立的初创公司投资 100 亿美元，该公司估值为 24 亿美元，而且只是刚刚秘密进行。

Volta 的想法是，在 Andreessen Horowitz、Altimeter、Nvidia 和 Michael Dell 的支持下，让更多人能够买得起 Nvidia 的芯片，而不仅仅是巨头。 它计划通过比特币矿商 Bitdeer 部分运行 Anthropic 的产能，从挪威的一个站点开始。

对于 Volta 来说，这笔交易既是验证也是压舱石。 价值 100 亿美元的主力客户为一家刚刚成立几天的初创公司提供了信誉和现金流，以供其融资和发展。

对于 Anthropic 来说，将计算分散到许多供应商是一种保险形式。 没有任何一家提供商能够满足其需求，并且过度依赖任何一方（包括其自己的投资者）本身就会带来风险。

多元化还涉及杠杆作用；一家可以在亚马逊、谷歌、AMD 之间转移工作负载的实验室，现在初创公司在价格或优先级上不再受制于其中任何一家。

Anthropic 甚至探索了构建自己的芯片，对于一家认为计算太重要而不能完全交给其他公司的公司来说，这是合乎逻辑的终点。

这些安排也加剧了整个人工智能热潮以来的担忧。 芯片制造商和云越来越多地帮助从他们那里购买产品的客户融资，这是一个相互关联的网络，如果需求令人失望，可能会扩大损失。

这一切的规模难以估量。 Anthropic 的计算承诺现已达到数百亿美元，押注对 Claude 的需求将继续快速攀升，足以证明支出是合理的。

支出跟踪业务。 随着 Claude 赢得了企业客户，Anthropic 的收入大幅攀升，这使得它签署了一些可能让一家小公司陷入困境的承诺。

向一家成立数天的公司投入 100 亿美元也并非没有风险。 Volta 仍然需要构建和交付，而 Anthropic 则有效地押注于初次运营商能够以现有云难以企及的规模执行任务。

这笔交易还暗示了目前的瓶颈所在。 Anthropic 不仅追求芯片，还追求运行芯片的电力和场地，而这正是像 Volta 这样由基础设施金融家建立的公司所销售的产品。

对于一家力争让克劳德保持领先地位的公司来说，数学很简单。 容量是制约因素，Anthropic 将把它带到任何它能找到的地方，即使是来自一年前还不存在的初创公司。
